uncited: Topology and Ambiguity Handling resolves the topological inconsistencies inherent in standard lookup-table-based isosurface extraction when the isosurface passes through saddle points within a voxel.

Standard lookup tables assign a fixed triangulation to ambiguous cases (e.g., 46, 47, 98, 99, 210, 213, 214, 215), which can cause cracks or holes if adjacent voxels resolve the ambiguity differently [S1].
The family addresses the ambiguous case problem where the 8-bit sign pattern of a voxel's vertices does not uniquely determine the isosurface topology.
In these configurations, the isosurface passes through the cube center, creating a saddle point [S1].

All methods in this family enforce local consistency across voxel boundaries to ensure the output mesh is a topological manifold, preventing cracks or non-manifold vertices that arise when adjacent voxels resolve the ambiguity inconsistently [S1].

The ambiguity problem arises because the standard 256-case lookup table uses a fixed triangulation for saddle-point configurations, which fails to distinguish between topologically distinct surfaces [S1].
